ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the line $DE$ parallel to $BC$ divides $\triangle ABC$ into two parts with an area ratio of 1$\colon$4. What is the value of $\frac{AD}{AB}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that line DE divides $\triangle ABC$ into two parts with an area ratio of 1:4,\\
it follows that $S_{\triangle ADE} = \frac{1}{5}S_{\triangle ABC}$,\\
Since DE$\parallel$BC,\\
it implies that $\triangle ADE \sim \triangle ABC$,\\
thus $\frac{S_{\triangle ADE}}{S_{\triangle ABC}}=\left(\frac{AD}{AB}\right)^2=\frac{1}{5}$,\\
therefore $\frac{AD}{AB}=\boxed{\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, A is above, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right; point D is on side AB, point E is on side AC, line segment DE crosses the triangle horizontally, and is parallel to the base BC, dividing the original triangle into the upper small triangle ADE and the lower trapezoidal region DBCE. Reasoning: According to the problem statement, DE divides triangle ABC into two parts with an area ratio of 1:4, therefore the area of the upper small triangle ADE accounts for 1/(1+4)=1/5 of the area of the entire triangle ABC. Because DE ∥ BC, triangle ADE and triangle ABC are similar, and the corresponding side ratio is AD/AB. The area ratio of similar triangles is equal to the square of the corresponding side-length ratio, so (AD/AB)^2 = S_△ADE/S_△ABC = 1/5. Taking the positive square root, AD/AB = 1/√5 = √5/5.
